central_unknown: F1 hasn't raced at Sepang since 2017 and no team planned for it at the start of the season — combined with a high probability of rain across all sessions, the learning curve and weather variance make qualifying order and race pace highly uncertain.

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli (C), Russell, Mercedes constructor, one of Ferrari/McLaren constructor
budget_tiers.fills: Hadjar, Lindblad/Lawson, Hulkenberg/Stroll at price floor

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli (C), Leclerc or Hamilton, Ferrari constructor
budget_tiers.fills: Hadjar, Colapinto/Bortoleto, Racing Bulls constructor, budget driver at floor

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: ML projects 24.7 exp pts (highest on the grid), 30.2 proj pts, ppm 1.93, LOW risk, DNF 0.04 — the safest and highest-ceiling captain pick. FanAmp and BoxBox channels consistently back Antonelli as the core asset to build around. Even if he had floor damage in a prior FP session, his upside at a power-rewarding track with Mercedes' strong PU is enormous.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 23.5 exp pts (3rd highest), pred quali P7 → finish P2 meaning massive overtake points potential, ppm 1.43, MEDIUM risk. FanAmp notes Red Bull Ford PU is particularly strong and sector 3 at Sepang favors power units. Low ownership differential upside vs. consensus Antonelli captain. Channels favor Antonelli but ML ranks Verstappen nearly equal on expected points with higher overtake upside.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: George Russell
captains.reason: ML projects 23.6 exp pts (2nd highest), highest proj pts at 37.3, pred quali P1 → finish P1, but MEDIUM risk with DNF 0.15. If you're not captaining Antonelli, Russell is the next best Mercedes option. Channels note Russell 'blitzed it' when he had nothing to lose.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: ML projects 10.3 exp pts, ppm 1.72 (elite value), pred P8→P8. Needs only -2 pts for price rise — near-guaranteed budget builder. BoxBox calls him a 'must-have' stopgap with A-tier car at B-tier price.

buy.name: Ollie Lindblad
buy.note: At or near price floor, needs only -5 pts for price rise. BoxBox lists him as a no-brainer budget builder. Cheap insurance to fund premium assets.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: BoxBox calls Lawson a 'no-brainer' transfer target. Needs only -3 pts for price rise. Racing Bulls constructor (exp 22.2 pts, value 1.45, LOW risk) supports both RB drivers.

buy.name: Franco Colapinto
buy.note: Needs only -8 pts for max price rise — the lowest threshold on the grid. Strong budget-building asset even if Alpine struggles for pace.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: FormulaFantasyHub highlights 9.1 avg pts/race, 6.4 overtakes/GP (2nd on grid), only 1 DNF all season. Boring but reliable mid-priced pick. Needs 8 pts for price rise — achievable but not guaranteed.

consider.name: Sergio Perez
consider.note: FormulaFantasyHub prefers Perez over Bottas for fantasy potential — shown double-digit scoring ability. At price floor. BoxBox warns about Cadillac reliability though.

consider.name: Oliver Bearman
consider.note: BoxBox considers him as a mid-tier option who could outscore Hulkenberg. Needs 6 pts for price rise.

avoid: Lance Stroll — 4 consecutive race retirements, 5 of last 6 DNFs; only useful as price-floor ballast at 3M
Valtteri Bottas — consistently slowest on pace, 30s behind teammate in Baku, Cadillac reliability dire; FormulaFantasyHub says hold only if already owned
Alex Albon — BoxBox says 'not touching with a 20-ft pole'; Williams performance not there this year
Carlos Sainz — ML projects negative points (P18 predicted in other weekends); poor value at 13M

chips.name: 3x Captain Boost
chips.reason: BoxBox activated 3x at Monza over Limitless because it scored higher in simulations (~380 vs 372 pts). If Mercedes dominance at Sepang is confirmed in FP sessions (as at Monza), 3x on Antonelli could be the play. Wait for FP3 data before committing.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: BoxBox analysis showed Limitless underperformed vs 3x boost at Monza. With budget-building opportunities abundant at Sepang, save Limitless for a sprint weekend or higher-certainty event.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: If you need to restructure for maximum budget building (bringing in Colapinto, Hadjar, Lindblad, Lawson, Racing Bulls constructor simultaneously), Wildcard could pay dividends. BoxBox notes pivoting to B-tier constructors for 0.6M rises vs 0.1-0.3M from A-tier constructors.

chips.name: 4A (Four Aces)
chips.reason: BoxBox activated 4A at Zandvoort for Ferrari+McLaren dominance. Sepang's uncertainty and rain risk make this a poor 4A weekend — save for a more predictable track.

watch_items: Rain probability across all sessions — wet weather could completely reshuffle the grid and neutralize car advantages, benefiting experienced wet-weather drivers like Hamilton and Verstappen
FP1-FP3 adaptation: with no team having raced here since 2017, watch who adapts quickest; Chris McCarthy notes confident drivers learn new circuits faster
McLaren's shorter gearbox ratio: Sepang has one of the highest acceleration-to-top-speed ratios of the remaining calendar, potentially benefiting Norris/Piastri significantly
Mercedes power unit advantage in sector 3 long straights — FanAmp's Terry flags Mercedes PU as strong at this track layout
Kimi Antonelli floor damage risk — had issues in a prior FP1; if repeated, could affect qualifying and reduce captain ceiling
Oscar Piastri form check — ML projects only 15.2 exp pts (P7 finish); channels suggest he could reset at a new circuit but recent form is poor
Budget building: Multiple drivers near price-rise thresholds with very low point requirements — prioritize guaranteed risers (Colapinto -8, Lindblad -5, Lawson -3, Hadjar -2)
arc: Sepang is the first of three races where McLaren's shorter gearbox should provide a significant advantage according to Ruth Buskcom's acceleration ratio analysis. This sets up a potential McLaren-heavy run through the end of the season. Budget building is critical now — with so many cheap drivers near price-rise thresholds, the transfers made at Sepang will determine whether managers can afford a full 4A lineup (four premium assets) in the coming weeks. Rain at Sepang could scramble results and create unexpected price movements, so managers with Wildcards in reserve gain flexibility. The Mercedes dominance flagged by ML (64.2 exp constructor pts, LOW risk) could carry into the next round if the PU advantage holds, making Antonelli + Russell a season-closing anchor pairing.
